title: NORD-10 I/O device card: connector to the backplane

sources.document: Backwiring til NORD-10 (A/S Norsk Data-Elektronikk): connector specification list, connector lists per card position, signal code list
sources.note: Typed wiring list of the NORD-10 CPU crate. The connector lists of A22 and A25 were checked against the page images; the OCR of the other slot pages agrees with them pin for pin.

sources.document: NORD-10 drawings, sheet 2A50 SYNCHRONOUS MODEM BUFFER 1050 (1973), as read pin by pin in this repository (sheets/nord-10/2A50-sync-modem-buffer-1050.rsc, docs/2A50-reading.md)
sources.note: The names the card drawing uses (LEV10, IOXE, MC ...) differ from the backplane names (BINT10, BIOXE, BMCL ...); the pin numbers match.

sources.document: ND-06.008.01 NORD-10/S Reference Manual, Revision A
sources.note: Sections 3.3 (IOX), IDENT instruction, 4.1 (Input/Output hardware) and 4.1.3 (vectored interrupt identification). It refers to the NORD-10 Input/Output manual ND-06.004 for signal levels, definitions and timing; that manual was NOT found on this machine.

sources.document: ND manual ND-06.012.01: figure 3.1 'I/O slot/plug layout' (page 3-3) and figure 7.4 'Signal distribution I/O bus B and C rack' (section 7.4)
sources.note: Read from the owner's screenshots of the two figures (2026-11-24); the rest of the manual has not been read here. name.note: Figure 3.1 shows one 100-terminal connector per I/O slot: 4 terminals for power (0, 1, 98, 99 = +5V) and 4 for ground (2, 3, 96, 97). The maker and part number of the backplane connector are OPEN. No A/B/C letters are used for it.

power.note: Figure 3.1: '4 terminals for power, 4 for ground'. The backwiring list names no supply pin (it lists signal wires only). 62/63 and 66/67 on 2A50 are outputs of the card's own +-12V converter on the cable side, not supply in, and the grounds 80, 82, 84, 86, 94 are 2A50's cable returns - the card's choice of free cable pins.

note: NORD-10/S manual section 4.1.1: 'Cable connectors are plugged directly into the backplane' and 'Device plugs are also to a common standard' (read). Every circled pin on 2A50, bus and modem alike, is a pin of this one 0-99 connector, written P.n (owner's decision 2026-11-23); 6-55 is the bus side, 56-99 the cable side (inferred). The former separate file nord10-modem-front.json is merged in here as the 81-95 rows.

pins.note: Figure 7.4 names pin 6 INIDENT, not IDENT out. Backwiring til NORD-10 has the chain the other way: IDENT1 0 = A25:G06 to A26:07 (G = the driving pin) and BIDENT from A22 into A25 pin 7, so pin 6 is the output there. The two sources DISAGREE; kept as the backwiring list has it until the page image or a card drawing settles it.

pins.description: IDENT search signal coming in from the card nearer the CPU. When several cards interrupt on the same level, the slot position decides priority; a card that answers IDENT turns off its interrupt.
pins.note: Figure 7.4 names pin 7 OUTIDENT, not IDENT in. Backwiring til NORD-10 feeds BIDENT from A22 into A25 pin 7, so pin 7 is the input there. The two sources DISAGREE; kept as the backwiring list has it.

fingers.value: 50 gold fingers on each side, 2.54 mm (0.1 inch) apart, each opposite one on the other side. Even pins on the component side, odd pins on the solder side: seen from the component side with the fingers at the top, finger k from the left (k = 0..49) is pin 2k, and the finger behind it on the solder side is pin 2k+1. So pin 0 and pin 1 are at the left end (component view), 98 and 99 at the right end.
fingers.source: photos of board 322049 (2A50), ND PCB catalogue; checked against the 2A50 drawing
proof: Count: 50 fingers on each side, measured on both new photos of 322049 (READ from the photos). Pitch 2.546 mm on the solder photo, 2.58 mm on the component photo (photo scale); 0.1 inch INFERRED.

Ground: on the component side the vias of fingers 40, 41, 42, 43 (counted from the left, from 0) are joined, and a wide trace joins 43 to 47. The drawing ties exactly five circled pins to ground: 80, 82, 84, 86, 94 = 2 x 40, 41, 42, 43, 47 (READ on the photo, matches the drawing).
BA0, pin 32: component finger 16 -> via -> solder-side trace -> via -> component trace -> 11C (7404, marked 7404 on the chip) pin 3. The drawing has BA0 = P.32 = 11C.3 (READ on the photos).
BA1, pin 33: the solder-side finger behind component finger 16 -> solder trace -> via -> component trace -> 11C pin 1. The drawing has BA1 = P.33 = 11C.1 (READ on the photos).

Use pattern: of the 50 solder-side fingers, 46 agree with "odd pin 2k+1 is used on 2A50 or not"; the next best rule (pins 2k on that side) agrees on 39, any 0-49 / 50-99 split on 27 or fewer. The four that disagree are pins 1 and 99 (wide copper at both ends: +5V, figure 3.1 of ND-06.012.01; not on the drawing), 9 (INGRANT, joined straight to pin 8) and 11 (IOXE, trace not followed to its end).
fingers.open: Whether every NORD-10 card follows the same rule (checked on 2A50 only); the finger length and width (about 8 mm and 1.5 mm, measured on one photo). The supply pins are no longer open: +5V 0, 1, 98, 99 and ground 2, 3, 96, 97 (ND-06.012.01 figure 3.1); the wide copper at 0, 1, 98, 99 on 2A50 matches. What the wide trace joining 60 and 64 on 2A50 is stays OPEN (cable side, not on the drawing).

cablePlug.value: Pins 56-95 go to the external device through a Berg plug on the card edge, cabled to a Burndy MS42RM plug in the plug panel.
cablePlug.note: Figure 3.1 shows Berg 56 -> Burndy v, 57 -> t, ... and 94/95 at the Burndy letters A-D; the figure is shown only in part, so the full Berg-to-Burndy letter table is OPEN. Where the Berg plug sits (on the backplane posts behind the slot, as the NORD-10/S manual's 'cable connectors are plugged directly into the backplane' suggests, or on the card itself) is not settled by the figure text as read; 96-99 are supply, not cable pins.

levels.value: tri-state TTL, except the interrupt lines and DMA request: open collector. Logical 1 = 0-0.4 V, logical 0 = 2.4-5 V (active low).
levels.page: figure 7.4 'Signal distribution I/O bus B and C rack', section 7.4
